text:
I want to talk about TWO technologies today that might make some people uncomfortable. 👀

$ICP and $KAS.

What if some of the most underestimated technologies in crypto are the ones the market simply isn't ready to understand yet?

$ICP is trying to build a World Computer — decentralized computing, on-chain applications, AI infrastructure and native cross-chain integration.

$KAS is taking a different path — fair launch, Proof-of-Work, BlockDAG architecture and now programmable applications.

Two completely different visions. One common problem:

THE TECHNOLOGY MAY BE MOVING FASTER THAN ADOPTION.

Bitcoin had years to prove its place in the world. These projects are still fighting to prove their value to a much wider audience.

Could either one eventually deliver something so significant that it changes how we compare crypto projects — even next to Bitcoin?

Maybe. Maybe not.

I'm not saying they'll beat BTC in price or market cap.

I'm saying the market might be underestimating what they're trying to build.

Sometimes, being early feels exactly like being wrong.

And sometimes, the world needs years to catch up with an idea.

$ICP × $KAS.

Remember these two names. 🔥

quotedTweet.text:
QUARTERLY REVIEW: Q3 2026

76 trades. +58.6R. Not one loss bigger than 1R.

Every quarter I close the books and look at the numbers without filters. Not to celebrate, not to punish myself. Just to see what is real.

This quarter the numbers told me something I didn't fully expect. Let's go through it.

THE QUARTER IN NUMBERS

July: 17 trades, +9.5R
August: 24 trades, +20.05R
September: 35 trades, +29.05R

Q3 total: 76 trades, +58.6R
36 wins, 24 losses, 16 break-evens
Win rate: 60% without BE

Three months, three green months, and each one better than the one before.

The year so far:
Q1: +28.3R
Q2: +55.2R
Q3: +58.6R
2026 to date: +142.1R, 9 months out of 9 green.

THE NUMBER I'M PROUDEST OF: -1R

Look at every single loss of the quarter. 24 of them.

Not one went beyond -1R.

12 losses hit the full stop at exactly -1R. The other 12 were cut early, before the stop, for a total of -4.65R. If they had all run to the full stop, they would have cost me 7.35R more.

Average loss: -0.69R.
Average win: +2.09R.

That's the whole game in two lines. My wins are three times my losses. I don't need to be right most of the time. I need my losses to stay small every time.

Warren Buffett put it simply: "Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget rule No. 1."

In trading you will lose money. Every week. The real version of the rule is this: never lose more than you decided to lose. 76 trades, zero exceptions.

THE TECHNICAL PART

Win rate alone tells you almost nothing about a trader. These are the numbers that tell you if an edge is real or just luck. I'll explain each one simply.

EXPECTANCY: +0.77R per trade
This is the average result of one trade, counting everything: wins, losses and break-evens. 58.6R made over 76 trades = 0.77R per trade.
In simple words: every time I click buy or sell, on average I make 0.77 times what I risk. Risk 100$, expect 77$ back on average. Not on every trade, on average over many.
That's why expectancy matters more than win rate. A trader who wins 40% of the time can beat one who wins 70% if his winners are big and his losers are small.

PROFIT FACTOR: 4.52
All the R I won (75.25R) divided by all the R I lost (16.65R).
In simple words: for every 1$ the market took from me, I took 4.5$ back. Above 1.5 is decent, above 2 is good.

MAX DRAWDOWN: -2.0R
The worst drop from my best point to my lowest point during the quarter, trade after trade.
In simple words: in 76 trades, the deepest hole I was ever in was 2R. If you risk 1% per trade, that's a 2% dip at the worst moment of the quarter.

MAX LOSING STREAK: 3
The longest run of losses in a row. Three.
In simple words: I never got to the 5th, 6th, 7th loss in a row, the place where most traders start revenge trading and blow up a month in one afternoon.

SHARPE RATIO: 0.51 (per trade)
It measures how much return you get for how bumpy the ride is. Average result divided by how much the results swing around.
In simple words: high Sharpe = steady results, low Sharpe = a rollercoaster. I calculate it per trade, so it's not comparable with the yearly Sharpe of a fund. I use it to compare me with myself, quarter after quarter.

SORTINO RATIO: 1.80 (per trade)
Same idea as Sharpe, but it only counts the bad swings, the losses. Big winners don't punish the score.
In simple words: Sharpe treats a +5R surprise and a -5R surprise as equally "risky". Sortino only worries about the -5R. And the most interesting thing of this review is the gap between the two: Sortino 1.80 vs Sharpe 0.51. It means almost all my swings come from the winners. My upside moves around a lot. My downside barely moves at all.

That's exactly what you want as a trader.

THE STORY BEHIND THE NUMBERS: BTC

Here is what I didn't fully expect.

BTC in July: -0.2R
BTC in August: +16.15R
BTC in September: +20.05R

QUARTERLY REVIEW: Q3 2026

76 trades. +58.6R. Not one loss bigger than 1R.

Every quarter I close the books and look at the numbers without filters. Not to celebrate, not to punish myself. Just to see what is real.

This quarter the numbers told me something I didn't fully expect. Let's go through it.

THE QUARTER IN NUMBERS

July: 17 trades, +9.5R
August: 24 trades, +20.05R
September: 35 trades, +29.05R

Q3 total: 76 trades, +58.6R
36 wins, 24 losses, 16 break-evens
Win rate: 60% without BE

Three months, three green months, and each one better than the one before.

The year so far:
Q1: +28.3R
Q2: +55.2R
Q3: +58.6R
2026 to date: +142.1R, 9 months out of 9 green.

THE NUMBER I'M PROUDEST OF: -1R

Look at every single loss of the quarter. 24 of them.

Not one went beyond -1R.

12 losses hit the full stop at exactly -1R. The other 12 were cut early, before the stop, for a total of -4.65R. If they had all run to the full stop, they would have cost me 7.35R more.

Average loss: -0.69R.
Average win: +2.09R.

That's the whole game in two lines. My wins are three times my losses. I don't need to be right most of the time. I need my losses to stay small every time.

Warren Buffett put it simply: "Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget rule No. 1."

In trading you will lose money. Every week. The real version of the rule is this: never lose more than you decided to lose. 76 trades, zero exceptions.

THE TECHNICAL PART

Win rate alone tells you almost nothing about a trader. These are the numbers that tell you if an edge is real or just luck. I'll explain each one simply.

EXPECTANCY: +0.77R per trade
This is the average result of one trade, counting everything: wins, losses and break-evens. 58.6R made over 76 trades = 0.77R per trade.
In simple words: every time I click buy or sell, on average I make 0.77 times what I risk. Risk 100$, expect 77$ back on average. Not on every trade, on average over many.
That's why expectancy matters more than win rate. A trader who wins 40% of the time can beat one who wins 70% if his winners are big and his losers are small.

PROFIT FACTOR: 4.52
All the R I won (75.25R) divided by all the R I lost (16.65R).
In simple words: for every 1$ the market took from me, I took 4.5$ back. Above 1.5 is decent, above 2 is good.

MAX DRAWDOWN: -2.0R
The worst drop from my best point to my lowest point during the quarter, trade after trade.
In simple words: in 76 trades, the deepest hole I was ever in was 2R. If you risk 1% per trade, that's a 2% dip at the worst moment of the quarter.

MAX LOSING STREAK: 3
The longest run of losses in a row. Three.
In simple words: I never got to the 5th, 6th, 7th loss in a row, the place where most traders start revenge trading and blow up a month in one afternoon.

SHARPE RATIO: 0.51 (per trade)
It measures how much return you get for how bumpy the ride is. Average result divided by how much the results swing around.
In simple words: high Sharpe = steady results, low Sharpe = a rollercoaster. I calculate it per trade, so it's not comparable with the yearly Sharpe of a fund. I use it to compare me with myself, quarter after quarter.

SORTINO RATIO: 1.80 (per trade)
Same idea as Sharpe, but it only counts the bad swings, the losses. Big winners don't punish the score.
In simple words: Sharpe treats a +5R surprise and a -5R surprise as equally "risky". Sortino only worries about the -5R. And the most interesting thing of this review is the gap between the two: Sortino 1.80 vs Sharpe 0.51. It means almost all my swings come from the winners. My upside moves around a lot. My downside barely moves at all.

That's exactly what you want as a trader.

text:
🚨🚨🚨 $KEEL — Survive or Die?
Keel (ex-Bitfarms) is pivoting from Bitcoin mining into an AI/HPC infrastructure landlord.

What they have:
•~2.2 GW power pipeline
•Secured power in key markets (PA, WA, Quebec)
•Flagship sites like Panther Creek (~350 MW+)
•Strong liquidity (~$800M+)
•Not a pure GPU flipper — more power + land owner
What they don’t have yet:
•Meaningful contracted HPC/AI revenue
•Signed long-term leases at scale
•First full sites online only expected in 2027

In the current cycle: The easy phase (get GPUs + announce capacity) is ending. The next phase rewards operators with real contracted revenue, secured power, and balance sheets strong enough to finish projects.

KEEL has the scarce asset (power). But without signed leases, it risks becoming stranded compute — half-built sites, expensive debt, and no customers.

Bottom line: Not dead. Not safe either. Survival depends on converting power into real, financeable leases soon. If they execute → potential survivor. If not → dilution, delay, or acquisition target.
High execution risk. Still early.

Not financial advice.

quotedTweet.text:
$NBIS $CRWV $IREN $CIFR $APLD

The most honest thing said about AI infrastructure this week did not come from an earnings call. It came from a lab insider: even if we fail to train the best model, we locked in GPU capacity early, rental prices are up two to three times, so we can just resell the compute and print money.

Read that again. The plan is not to build something better. The plan is to flip rented GPUs. That is not a business model, it is an arbitrage, and every arbitrage in history ends the same way: supply floods in, prices fall, the music stops, and whoever is left holding the contracts takes the loss.

Musk sees it too. Consolidation next year, most will not survive, and a lot of stranded compute sitting in partially complete data centers. Think about what that means: buildings half-finished, GPUs ordered, power not yet connected, customers not yet signed, all financed with expensive debt. When the financing gets dear and the customers do not show up on schedule, those projects do not get completed, they get stranded.

This is the part of the cycle where the trade changes character. The first phase rewarded anyone who could get GPUs and announce capacity. The next phase rewards only the operators with contracted revenue, real customers, secured power, and a balance sheet strong enough to finish what they started. Everyone else becomes someone else's acquisition, or nothing at all.

None of this kills the compute thesis. The buildout is real and it is still early. But the winners narrow sharply from here, and the gap between owning infrastructure with demand behind it and owning a GPU-flipping story is about to get very expensive for the wrong side. Shakeouts feel brutal in the moment, but they are how a real industry gets built. The survivors come out of them stronger, and the next phase belongs to them.

Educational only, not financial advice.

Hot take: the most important WBTC news this month has nothing to do with price.

On Oct 7, @WrappedBTC announced it's exploring a multi-custodian model for its Bitcoin reserves.
